title: Evidence and project delivery
goal: Rebuild from saved source, verify the exact report bytes and deliver a reproducible package.

prerequisites.text: Prepare main.c, inventory.c, inventory.h, the input file and a set of check commands. Keep the reference and your own version separate.

terms.title: Reproducible build
terms.definition: A fresh compiler run with saved source and the header, using a recorded command.

terms.title: Run artifact
terms.definition: A file the program creates in its run workspace. Save or download it if you want to use it later.

sections.title: Rebuild without old object files
paragraphs: Before delivery, restore the project in a new folder. Build with clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.c inventory.c -o inventory. Keep inventory.h in the same folder and record the compiler version. A binary from an older build is not used.

Compare stdout, stderr, exit status and files separately. In summary.tsv TAB separates header fields and values and LF ends each row. A repeat report replaces the previous contents. Mode wb truncates on open. It cannot guarantee preservation of the old report if writing later fails.

In Code Studio, save your source files and the output file separately after a successful run. The file from a run is returned separately from the project. Use the explicit download or save action and verify that reopening restores your own files.

sections.title: Reproduce the ordinary run from a clean build
paragraphs: In a fresh folder, records.tsv contains items 10 and 20. After building, run the three commands from the first lesson. Record the exit status, stderr and example-summary.tsv contents separately. Your independent project uses summary.tsv.
steps: Build from both .c files and check the compiler output.
Run find 10, set 20 7 and report. The three stdout lines end with reported. Status is 0 and stderr is empty.
Compare the artifact separately and repeat against an empty inventory. Only the header should remain.

sections.title: Where to look for the cause
paragraphs: If the build works only in an old folder, check that inventory.c is included on the command line. If status is 0 but stale content remains, inspect the file bytes and the fopen mode.

sections.title: Test your prediction with a new input
paragraphs: Deliver the source, sample input files, build command, a report and a comparison log. Document the limit of 64 records, that the program does not persist changed quantities to records.tsv, and what can happen on a failed report write.
Include the exact commands and the observed report in the submission. A screenshot of reported alone does not verify the header, tabs, line feeds, and absence of stale rows.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Compare the listed C17 rules with their use in this project.

selfcheck.prompt: The program printed reported. How do you confirm that the finished file is available after closing the tab?
options: Save or download the file, reopen it and compare the bytes.
feedback: That confirms completion within the current run.
You have a separate observation that the artifact survives.
Source and output are stored separately.

selfcheck.prompt: A new report opened the existing file in wb mode, wrote some bytes and then failed. What can you promise about the previous report?
options: The file may be partial. Recovery needs a separately saved previous copy.
fclose always restores the previous bytes.
Exit status 3 rolls back the file by itself.
feedback: Opening with wb can already remove old data. Inspect the file and use the saved copy.
fclose closes the stream and may report an error, but cannot restore the previous bytes.
The status indicates failure. Version recovery needs a separate mechanism.

selfcheck.prompt: What check distinguishes accidental append from correct replacement when both runs exit with 0?
selfcheck.feedback: Start with a deliberately different old summary.tsv and compare the whole file after report. A stale prefix or second header proves appending.

cases.label: Two reports in a single run
A new run has its own state

practice.title: Deliver a report for the next shift
practice.task: Fix the summary.tsv open mode in the starter, which appends a report after a stale row. Rebuild in a fresh folder and run an ordinary report, empty input, an invalid command and a repeat report. Save your own package and reopen it.

steps.action: Build and check the supplied stale file.
steps.why: Stdout alone cannot reveal the wrong open mode.
steps.expected: The starter prints reported but keeps stale inventory before the header.

steps.action: Choose wb and run the full set of controls.
steps.why: A successful write must produce just the new header and current records.
steps.expected: The stale prefix disappears and two report calls can replace the same file within one run.

steps.action: Save the source and report separately, then build from the restored files.
steps.why: You can now reproduce both the result and the way you got it.
steps.expected: Stdout, stderr, status and report bytes agree. No personal data is needed.

criteria: The stale prefix is gone. After two report commands in one run, the final file has one header and the state from the most recent update.
With an empty records.tsv the report has just its header. After an invalid command, the later report does not execute.
The package contains three source files, fixtures and rebuild instructions. State how you checked restoration of the run artifact.
practice.hint: Compare the whole file including its first and last bytes. Check fopen and fclose before claiming the report succeeded.

exercises.title: One more check
exercises.task: Add your own regression case that fails on the starter and passes on your fix. Record its input, expected streams, status and file. Explain the limitation of wb.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

teaching.scene: Package the project so a teammate can reopen it in a clean folder, build it, and reproduce the report. Verify the source, input TSV, commands, and output file separately.

predict.prompt: The example runs find 10, set 20 7, and report. What goes in example-summary.tsv? Does set change records.tsv?
predict.answer: The header id TAB quantity is followed by 10 TAB 5 and 20 TAB 7 with LF. set changes the state in memory. records.tsv still has quantity 0 for item 20. reported appears after writing and closing the report.

apply.prompt: With the same input, run report, set 10 0, then report in one session. Which lines remain in the file after the second report, and what does stdout show?
apply.answer: stdout contains reported, ok, reported. After the second report the file has one header, 10 TAB 0, and 20 TAB 0. Mode wb replaces the previous bytes. A fresh run with the original records.tsv starts with quantity 5 for item 10.

practice.strategy: Record both source files, the header, input file, and commands. Start with a stale summary.tsv, then verify two reports in sequence. Save the package and check it after reopening.
practice.diagnosis: If reported appears but the file begins with stale inventory or repeats its header, compare the whole file and inspect the open mode. If a clean build cannot find inventory_set, check whether inventory.c was included.

syntax.form:
FILE *output = fopen(path, "wb");
/* Check the open, writes, and close. */
syntax.explanation: Mode wb creates the file or truncates an existing one at open and writes in binary mode. This controls the stream. Saving the project package is an editor operation.
syntax.mistake: Mode ab adds bytes after the existing contents. Correct text at the end can hide stale data at the beginning.
